propose.instructions: The transcript is live speech recognition that stops at the latest recognized word. Numbered markers such as [1] sit between the newest words. Which marker is the last point where the speaker has finished a sentence or a self-contained clause, so that an interpreter could translate everything before it right now? The speaker may still be talking after the last marker.

criteria.none: No marker ends a sentence or self-contained clause; the speaker is still inside one.
criteria.1: Everything before [1] ends a sentence or self-contained clause.
criteria.2: Everything before [2] ends a sentence or self-contained clause.

verify.instructions: `before` is live speech recognition and `after` is what the speaker said next. Does `before` end exactly where a sentence or a self-contained clause ends, so that `before` can be translated without the words in `after`?

criteria.true: `before` ends a complete sentence or clause; `after` starts a new one.
criteria.false: `after` continues the sentence or clause that `before` ends with.
